key_insight: A frozen, general-purpose LLM can propose promising quantum circuit parameters for structured Hamiltonians, but performs worse than Adam optimization on general random Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: LLM-generated circuit parameters offer independently evaluable energy estimates, unlike direct energy predictions that may violate physical bounds.
method: Generate complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions.
Optionally refine parameters using iterative energy feedback.
Evaluate random, structured parent, and molecular Hamiltonians; probe blind circuit interpretation.
evidence_signal: Evaluations found larger energy errors than Adam for general Hamiltonians, limited gains from feedback, and promising low-energy configurations for structured Hamiltonians.
watch_item: Do not assume reliable optimization across problems; independently evaluate generated parameters and check direct energy predictions against spectral bounds.
paper_title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
